statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-74860 is a double free in the SAX attributeDecl callback of the libxml2 Python bindings (pythonAttributeDecl in python/libxml.c): after adding each enumerated attribute value to a list with PyList_SetItem, the handler also called Py_DECREF on it, so a document with a crafted DTD crashes a Python application that uses the SAX bindings (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-74860, https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/issues/1076). Upstream fixed it in libxml2 2.15.3 by removing that Py_DECREF: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/f41e1865781f74d1cadfe2fbdfeefed946026f12. The libxml2 2.9.14 code that Debian 13 ships still has the extra Py_DECREF, and Debian lists trixie as vulnerable. The DHI Debian 13 libxml2 source builds the Python bindings into the python3-libxml2 package and backports the upstream fix. The build of 2.1+deb13u3 that this range marks fixed, the only build of this source now in the DHI Debian repository, carries it on amd64 and arm64: its shipped changelog (/usr/share/doc/python3-libxml2/changelog.Debian.gz) records the backport for CVE-2026-74860, and disassembly of pythonAttributeDecl in the libxml2mod extension module, located with the python3-libxml2-dbgsym symbols, shows no reference-count decrement between the PyList_SetItem call and the next loop iteration. Earlier DHI builds of this source, no longer published, were built without the fix, except one earlier build of 2.1+deb13u3 that first added it; that build sorts below this boundary and reads as affected.
